home.how.title: How It Works
home.how.sub: Three steps, under a minute — whether it's two friends or a whole bar.
home.step1.title: Start a Room
home.step1.desc: One tap gets you a room code and QR — no accounts, no downloads, no sign-ups. Add the first song yourself or share the code around. And if you step away mid-night, your room and its queue are right where you left them.
home.step2.title: Everyone Adds Songs
home.step2.desc: Anyone in the room scans the code and searches YouTube from their own phone, dropping songs into the shared queue. Karaoke mode finds the best versions automatically.
home.step3.title: Sing on Any Screen
home.step3.desc: Open the display on whatever everyone's facing — TV, laptop, projector, tablet. Lyrics light up as you sing, the host steers the queue, and a QR code lets latecomers jump in.
home.setup.title: What You Need to Host
home.setup.sub: Less than you think — a screen with a browser and something that makes sound. Three ways people run it:
home.setup.card1.title: Just a Laptop or iPad
home.setup.card1.desc: Open KaraoQ, turn up the volume, and you're hosting. The video plays right on the device while everyone queues songs from their phones. Plug in a Bluetooth speaker if the room gets loud.
home.setup.card1.gear1: A laptop, iPad, or any device with a browser
home.setup.card2.title: The Living Room TV
home.setup.card2.desc: Put the song on the big screen — cast with AirPlay or Google Cast, or plug your laptop into the TV with HDMI. The TV's speakers carry the sound, and your device stays the control booth.
home.setup.card3.title: Screen + Sound System
home.setup.card3.desc: Run a laptop into the venue's display and sound system — HDMI to the screen, aux to the speakers. Guests add songs from their phones all night, and mics go through the PA like any other karaoke night.
home.setup.note.strong: No karaoke machine, no microphones required.
home.setup.note.rest: KaraoQ puts the song and lyrics on screen; sound comes from whatever's playing the video. Most living rooms just sing out loud — and if you have mics, run them through your speakers and you're a full venue.

home.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
home.faq.sub: Everything you need to know before your first song.
home.cta.title: Ready to Sing?
home.cta.sub: Start a karaoke session in seconds. No sign-up required.
faq.free.a: Yes. KaraoQ is free to host and free to join. Songs play from YouTube, so there is nothing to buy or rent.
faq.app.q: Do I need to download an app?
faq.app.a: No downloads and no installs. KaraoQ runs entirely in your web browser on phones, tablets, laptops, and smart TVs.
faq.equipment.q: What equipment do I need to host karaoke night?
faq.equipment.a: A device with a browser and something that makes sound — a laptop or iPad on its own is enough. For a bigger night, put the video on a TV by casting or plugging in with HDMI. No karaoke machine or microphones required.
faq.mics.q: Do I need a microphone for karaoke?
faq.mics.a: No. KaraoQ puts the song and the lyrics on screen, and plenty of living rooms just sing along out loud. A microphone is the upgrade that makes it feel like a real karaoke night — a cheap wireless pair plugged into a Bluetooth speaker's mic input is the setup most people land on. Run the mic through the speaker rather than pairing it to the TV, so voices and backing track come out of the same box and stay in sync.
faq.tv.q: How do I get the karaoke video on my TV?
faq.tv.a: Cast your screen with AirPlay or Google Cast, or connect your laptop to the TV with an HDMI cable. KaraoQ can also pop the video out into its own window, so the TV shows the song and lyrics while the controls stay on your screen.
faq.account.q: Do my guests need an account to sing?
faq.account.a: No sign-up is required for anyone. Guests scan a QR code or enter the room code, then start adding songs from their own phones.
faq.join.q: How do guests join the karaoke session?
faq.join.a: Create a room to get a short join code and QR code. Share either one, and guests can search YouTube and queue songs from their phones in seconds.
faq.songs.q: Where do the karaoke songs come from?
faq.songs.a: Every song streams from YouTube, so you have millions of karaoke tracks, lyric videos, and instrumentals to choose from — no separate karaoke library needed.
faq.venue.q: Can I use KaraoQ at a bar, party, or venue?
faq.venue.a: Absolutely. Cast the queue to any screen and let guests add songs from their phones. It works just as well for house parties, team events, and venue karaoke nights.

guide.athome.title: How to Host Karaoke at Home — No Machine Needed | KaraoQ
guide.athome.metaDesc: Host karaoke at home with nothing but a browser. Search YouTube, let guests queue songs from their phones, and put the lyrics on any screen — no karaoke machine, no downloads.
guide.athome.h1: How to host karaoke at home
guide.athome.intro: You don't need a karaoke machine, a subscription, or a stack of discs to throw a great karaoke night at home. With KaraoQ, any laptop, tablet, or phone becomes the whole setup: you search YouTube for the songs everyone already loves, guests add them to a shared queue from their own phones, and the lyrics play on whatever screen you have. Here's how to set it up in a couple of minutes.
guide.athome.step1.title: Open a room on any device
guide.athome.step1.body: Go to KaraoQ in your browser and create a room. There's nothing to download and no account to make — you get a short join code and a QR code straight away.
guide.athome.step2.title: Share the code so guests can join
guide.athome.step2.body: Show the QR code or read out the room code. Guests scan or type it on their own phones and they're in — no app, no sign-up, and nothing to set up on their end.
guide.athome.step3.title: Build the queue from everyone's phones
guide.athome.step3.body: Everyone searches YouTube from their phone and adds songs to one shared queue. KaraoQ plays them in order, so there's no fighting over the laptop and no one hogs the mic.
guide.athome.step4.title: Put the words on the biggest screen
guide.athome.step4.body: Cast your screen to the TV with AirPlay or Google Cast, plug in with an HDMI cable, or just prop up the laptop. KaraoQ can pop the video into its own window so the lyrics fill the screen while you keep the controls on your phone.
guide.athome.closing: That's it — no machine, no library, no clutter. As long as one device has a browser and something that makes sound, you can host karaoke anywhere: a living room, a dorm, a backyard, or a hotel room on a trip.
guide.tv.title: How to Do Karaoke on Your TV — Cast, HDMI or Pop-Out | KaraoQ
guide.tv.metaDesc: Get karaoke lyrics on your TV in minutes. Cast from your phone, connect a laptop with HDMI, or pop the video into its own window — while everyone queues songs from their phones.
guide.tv.h1: How to do karaoke on your TV
guide.tv.intro: A TV turns a phone-sized karaoke session into a proper show — big lyrics everyone can read from across the room. KaraoQ works with whatever you already have: a smart TV, a streaming stick, or a plain HDMI cable. Here are the three easy ways to get the song and the words on the big screen.
guide.tv.step1.title: Cast from your phone or laptop
guide.tv.step1.body: If you have a smart TV, Chromecast, or Apple TV, use Google Cast or AirPlay to mirror your screen. Open KaraoQ's display view, cast it, and the queue and lyrics show up on the TV instantly.
guide.tv.step2.title: Or plug in with an HDMI cable
guide.tv.step2.body: No casting? Connect a laptop to the TV with an HDMI cable and pick the TV as your screen. It's the most reliable option and needs no Wi-Fi or setup at all.
guide.tv.step3.title: Use pop-out so controls stay on your phone
guide.tv.step3.body: KaraoQ can pop the karaoke video into its own window. Put that window on the TV and keep the host controls — queue, skip, reactions — on your phone or laptop, so you never have to walk up to the screen mid-song.
guide.tv.step4.title: Let guests add songs from their seats
guide.tv.step4.body: While the TV shows the current song, everyone else searches YouTube and queues their next pick from their own phones. The lineup builds itself and the show never stops between songs.
guide.tv.closing: Whether you cast, plug in, or pop out, the TV only ever shows the song and lyrics — the controls stay private on your device. That's karaoke on the big screen without a single piece of dedicated hardware.
guide.youtube.title: Free YouTube Karaoke — Millions of Songs, No Downloads | KaraoQ
guide.youtube.metaDesc: Turn YouTube into a free karaoke library. Search millions of karaoke tracks and lyric videos, build a shared queue from your phone, and sing — no subscription, no downloads.
guide.youtube.h1: Free YouTube karaoke for any party
guide.youtube.intro: YouTube is the biggest karaoke library in the world — millions of instrumentals, lyric videos, and karaoke tracks, all free. KaraoQ turns that library into a real karaoke night: searchable, queued, and shared across everyone's phones. No subscription, no app, and no catalog to buy.
guide.youtube.step1.title: Search the songs everyone knows
guide.youtube.step1.body: Type any song into KaraoQ and it searches YouTube for the best karaoke and lyric versions. From throwback pop to the latest hits in any language, if it's on YouTube, it's ready to sing.
guide.youtube.step2.title: Add to one shared queue
guide.youtube.step2.body: Every guest adds songs from their own phone to a single shared queue. KaraoQ plays them back to back in order, so the night flows without anyone touching the laptop.
guide.youtube.step3.title: Sing along to the words on screen
guide.youtube.step3.body: The song streams straight from YouTube with the lyrics right there on screen — on a phone, a laptop, or cast to the TV. Nothing to install and nothing to rip or download.
guide.youtube.step4.title: Keep it free from start to finish
guide.youtube.step4.body: KaraoQ is free to host and free to join, and the songs are free because they play from YouTube. There's nothing to buy, rent, or subscribe to — just open a room and start singing.
guide.youtube.closing: Because it's all YouTube, your karaoke library is effectively endless and always up to date with the songs people actually want to sing. It's the simplest, cheapest way to run karaoke for a party — and it costs nothing.
guide.venue.title: Karaoke for Bars & Venues — Guests Queue From Their Phones | KaraoQ
guide.venue.metaDesc: Run karaoke at your bar or venue without a KJ or a dedicated machine. Guests scan a QR code, queue songs from their phones, and sing to any screen. Free to run, nothing to install.
guide.venue.h1: Karaoke for bars, parties and venues
guide.venue.intro: Running karaoke at a bar, party, or event usually means a host, a laptop full of files, and a line of people waiting to hand over a slip of paper. KaraoQ replaces all of it: guests queue their own songs from their phones, the lineup manages itself, and the words play on any screen you already have. Here's how to run a karaoke night that scales to a full room.
guide.venue.step1.title: Put a QR code on the tables
guide.venue.step1.body: Create a room and print or display the QR code and join code. Guests scan it from anywhere in the room and join instantly — no app to download and no account to create.
guide.venue.step2.title: Let guests queue their own songs
guide.venue.step2.body: Everyone searches YouTube and adds songs from their own phone. The shared queue keeps every turn in order, so staff never have to run a paper list or babysit a laptop.
guide.venue.step3.title: Show the lineup on your screens
guide.venue.step3.body: Cast or plug KaraoQ into the venue's TV or projector. The screen shows the current singer, the lyrics, and who's up next, so the whole room can follow along.
guide.venue.step4.title: Keep the energy up with reactions
guide.venue.step4.body: Guests cheer and react from their phones, and reactions light up the screen in real time. It turns a quiet open mic into a room that's actually into it — with no extra staff.
guide.venue.closing: KaraoQ is free to run and needs no dedicated karaoke machine, so it works just as well for a weekly bar night, a private party, or a one-off event. Set up a room, share the code, and let the room run its own karaoke.
guide.gear.title: Cheap Home Karaoke Setup — What You Actually Need | KaraoQ
guide.gear.metaDesc: Build a home karaoke setup on a budget: the software is free (KaraoQ + YouTube), so your money goes to a mic and a speaker. Here's the short shopping list and what to skip.
guide.gear.h1: The cheap home karaoke setup that actually works
guide.gear.intro: The secret to cheap home karaoke is that the expensive part — the songs and the machine — is now free. KaraoQ plays millions of karaoke tracks straight from YouTube in your browser, so the whole software side costs nothing. That leaves just the physical bits: something to hear the music on, something to sing into, and a screen for the lyrics. You probably own half of it already. Here's what's actually worth buying, and what you can skip.
guide.gear.step1.title: Start with what's free: the screen and the songs
guide.gear.step1.body: Open KaraoQ in a browser and you have the song library, the shared queue, and the lyrics display handled. Any TV, laptop, tablet, or even a phone propped on the coffee table works as the lyrics screen — spend nothing here until you know you need more.
guide.gear.step2.title: Sort out the sound
guide.gear.step2.body: TV speakers are fine for a first night, but a Bluetooth party speaker is the single biggest upgrade you can make — vocals and backing track fill the room instead of coming out of a thin TV panel. If the speaker has a microphone input, even better: that one box becomes your whole PA.
guide.gear.step3.title: Add microphones
guide.gear.step3.body: Wireless karaoke mics usually come in pairs, which matters more than specs — duets are half the fun. Plug the receiver into your speaker's mic input (or use a mic with its own built-in speaker) rather than pairing the mic to the TV, so voices stay in sync with the music.
guide.gear.step4.title: Get the lyrics on the big screen
guide.gear.step4.body: Cast KaraoQ from your laptop or phone with AirPlay or Google Cast, plug in with an HDMI cable, or use a streaming stick on any older TV. A cable is the zero-lag, zero-fuss option; casting means no wires across the living room. Either way, guests keep queuing songs from their own phones.
guide.gear.itemsIntro: Six things, roughly in order of impact. The first two or three are all most living rooms ever need — the rest is polish.
guide.gear.item1.name: Wireless karaoke microphones (2-pack)
guide.gear.item1.body: The heart of the setup. A two-pack covers duets and pass-the-mic moments, and most come with both a receiver for your speaker and built-in speakers of their own for a zero-setup option.
guide.gear.item2.name: Bluetooth party speaker
guide.gear.item2.body: Pick one with a microphone input and you've built a karaoke PA for the price of a speaker. Battery-powered models move to the garden or the garage with the party.
guide.gear.item3.name: HDMI cable (10 ft)
guide.gear.item3.body: The unglamorous hero: laptop to TV, done. No lag, no dropped connection mid-chorus, no fiddling with casting while everyone waits. Ten feet reaches the couch.
guide.gear.item4.name: Streaming stick with casting
guide.gear.item4.body: If your TV is older or your laptop needs to stay in the kitchen with the snacks, a streaming stick puts a castable screen on any HDMI port. Also the tidiest option for a permanent setup.
guide.gear.item5.name: Adjustable tablet stand
guide.gear.item5.body: Turns a spare tablet into a singer's monitor — lyrics at eye height instead of everyone craning at the TV. Also great for propping up the host phone running the room.
guide.gear.item6.name: All-in-one karaoke machine (optional)
guide.gear.item6.body: Speaker, mic inputs, and lights in one box. Skip it for a first night — but if karaoke becomes your thing, one of these plus KaraoQ as the song library is a seriously capable setup.
guide.gear.faq1.q: How much does a home karaoke setup cost?
guide.gear.faq1.a: As little as nothing: KaraoQ and its YouTube song library are free, so a TV and a phone are technically a complete setup. A pair of wireless mics and a party speaker — the setup most people land on — is typically well under the cost of a single karaoke machine, and there's no subscription on top.
guide.gear.faq2.q: Do I need a karaoke machine?
guide.gear.faq2.a: No. A karaoke machine bundles a speaker, mic inputs, and a song catalog — but the catalog is the part that used to cost money, and YouTube made it free. A Bluetooth speaker with a mic input does the same job, and KaraoQ replaces the catalog, the queue, and the lyrics screen.
guide.gear.faq3.q: What's the cheapest way to get lyrics on the TV?
guide.gear.faq3.a: An HDMI cable from a laptop — often one you already own. Next cheapest is casting with AirPlay or Google Cast if your TV supports it, which costs nothing at all. A streaming stick is only needed for older TVs that can't do either.
guide.gear.faq4.q: Why do the vocals lag behind the music on my wireless mic?
guide.gear.faq4.a: That happens when the mic pairs to the TV over Bluetooth — the audio round-trip adds a delay. Route the mic into the speaker instead (via the receiver or a cable), or use a mic with its own built-in speaker. Voice and backing track then come out of the same box, in sync.
guide.gear.closing: Total damage for a setup that handles birthdays, holidays, and random Tuesday nights: a mic two-pack, a speaker, and maybe a cable. The song library, the queue, and the lyrics screen stay free forever — that part's on us.
guide.channels.title: The 6 Best YouTube Karaoke Channels for Free Karaoke | KaraoQ
guide.channels.metaDesc: The YouTube karaoke channels actually worth knowing — Sing King, KaraFun, Stingray, Party Tyme, Sing2Piano, and CC Karaoke — and how to turn them into a real karaoke night with a shared queue.
guide.channels.intro: YouTube quietly became the biggest karaoke library on earth — but the quality lives on a handful of dedicated channels that professionally produce backing tracks with on-screen lyrics. These six cover almost any song a party can throw at you. Search inside KaraoQ and their tracks show up automatically; queue them from everyone's phones and the night runs itself.
guide.channels.itemsIntro: Ordered roughly by how often they'll save your party. Between them: pop, rock, country, showtunes, and every wedding-reception staple ever written.
guide.channels.item1.name: Sing King
guide.channels.item1.body: The heavyweight — the biggest dedicated karaoke channel on YouTube, with thousands of polished tracks and new hits added fast. If a song was ever on the radio, Sing King probably has it, with clean instrumentals and crisp lyric timing.
guide.channels.item2.name: KaraFun
guide.channels.item2.body: The YouTube arm of the KaraFun karaoke company, so the production quality is studio-grade: faithful re-recordings, backing vocals where the original needs them, and reliable lyric sync across a huge catalog.
guide.channels.item3.name: Stingray Karaoke
guide.channels.item3.body: Formerly The Karaoke Channel — one of the oldest licensed karaoke libraries anywhere, now under the Stingray banner. Deep coverage of classics, country, and standards that younger channels skip, with proper scrolling lyrics.
guide.channels.item4.name: Party Tyme Karaoke
guide.channels.item4.body: Radio-quality backing tracks from Sybersound, a name karaoke bars have trusted for decades. Especially strong on decades hits and crowd-pleasers — the songs the whole room sings along to.
guide.channels.item5.name: Sing2Piano
guide.channels.item5.body: Piano-only backing tracks, and secretly the best channel for nervous singers — a solo piano is far more forgiving than a full arrangement. Also the go-to for stripped-back versions of big ballads.
guide.channels.item6.name: CC Karaoke
guide.channels.item6.body: A smaller creator-run channel with a devoted following, focused on doing karaoke properly: accurate lyrics, sensible keys, and current songs that the big channels haven't covered yet.
guide.channels.faq1.a: Yes. These channels publish their tracks free on YouTube, and KaraoQ plays them straight from YouTube at no cost — free to host, free to join, no subscription. You'll see the occasional ad, same as YouTube anywhere.
guide.channels.faq2.q: How do I run a party off these channels?
guide.channels.faq2.a: Create a KaraoQ room and share the QR code. Everyone searches from their own phone — results pull in tracks from all of these channels — and adds songs to one shared queue that plays back to back on your TV. No more passing a laptop around.
guide.channels.faq3.q: What if a song isn't on any karaoke channel?
guide.channels.faq3.a: Search the song name plus "karaoke" or "instrumental" — smaller channels cover an astonishing long tail. Failing that, a lyric video of the original works surprisingly well for songs everyone half-knows anyway.
guide.channels.faq4.q: Can I play these channels on my TV?
guide.channels.faq4.a: Yes — cast KaraoQ to the TV with AirPlay or Google Cast, plug in over HDMI, or use a streaming stick. The lyrics play full-screen while the queue keeps running from everyone's phones.
guide.channels.closing: Subscribe to a couple of these and your karaoke library updates itself forever — no discs, no downloads, no fees. Then let KaraoQ do the rest: one shared queue, everyone picking from their own phone, lyrics on the big screen.
